sources.title: History
sources.supports: Alþing established around 930; Commonwealth period ending with submission beginning in 1262.

sources.title: Althingi: parliamentary information booklet
sources.locator: Printed pp. 6–9: Historical background, The monarchy until 1800, Sovereign state, Republic
sources.supports: Old Covenant process 1262–1264; later Danish monarchy; parliamentary institutions; sovereignty on 1 December 1918; republic on 17 June 1944.

sources.title: Velkommen statsborger i Norge — Historien
sources.supports: Danish–Norwegian union dated 1380–1814; institutional change after 1536–1537. The overlay names the shared crown broadly, without implying unchanged constitutional arrangements.

sources.title: Nú er tíð að vakna: Kristján Friðrik og sjálfstæðisbarátta Noregs og Íslands
sources.locator: Gunnar Pálsson, 27 May 2014; paragraphs on Kílarsamningurinn
sources.supports: January 1814 Treaty of Kiel: Iceland, Greenland and the Faroes remained connected to Denmark when Norway was ceded.

sources.title: Centennial of the Danish–Icelandic Union Act of 1918
sources.locator: Elin Hofverberg, 29 November 2018; opening and What Made the 1918 Union Act Special?
sources.supports: 1874 constitution, home rule effective in 1904, sovereign personal union effective 1 December 1918.

sources.title: Picturing a Nation: Capturing the Founding of the Republic in 1944
The Icelandic Minister (Thors) to the Secretary of State, 17 June 1944
sources.institution: Icelandic Government; published in US Department of State, FRUS 1944, vol. III, document 915
sources.supports: Republican constitution entered into force on 17 June 1944; election of Sveinn Björnsson.

sources.title: The Department of State to the British Embassy
sources.institution: US Department of State, FRUS 1944, vol. III, document 907
sources.supports: Independent state since 1918; the 1941 defence agreement explicitly respected Icelandic independence and sovereignty.

sources.title: The Icelandic Ministry for Foreign Affairs to the American Legation in Iceland
sources.institution: Iceland Ministry for Foreign Affairs; published in US Department of State, FRUS 1943, vol. II, document 277
sources.supports: British occupation began 10 May 1940; 1941 defence arrangements provided for American forces to supplement and replace them. Military presence is distinct from sovereignty.
